## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: when the command adopts a setting, it now prints the adoption message twice. `plan` already emits it as progress, and `cli.run` now prints it again from the new `adopt` change entry. The audit-entry part of the change works as described and is tested.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Running the command with a setting that already exists, e.g. `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, messages.append)`, now produces `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]` instead of one progress line. `plan` still calls `emit(f"Adopted {name}")` at app/planner.py:8, and the new `{"kind": "adopt", ...}` entry is then emitted again by `app/cli.py:6-9`, which skips only `kind == "audit"`. Before this change, adopt records were not in `changes`, so only the progress line was printed. The PR body says the command "continues to render actionable changes," so the fix is either to make `cli.run` skip `kind == "adopt"` as it skips audit entries, or to drop the progress `emit` in `plan`. Either way, add a `run`-level adoption test that asserts the exact `messages` list: today `test_adoption_progress` calls `plan` directly and `test_command_adds_setting` covers only the add path, so no test catches this. — Every adoption run shows duplicate "Adopted …" lines to command users, and no test guards against it.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_audit_is_returned_without_command_output` checks two behaviors through the public `run` entry point: the audit record is returned, and it is not printed.
